author: Etan Kissling
subject: Track support from empty slots and from equivocating validators for FCR (#8026)
body:
* Track support from empty slots and from equivocating validators for FCR

Fast Confirmation Rule requires weights collected during empty slots,
and also needs to know effective balances of equivocating validators.
Collect that info in one call (get_ancestor_support_by_slot) rather
than having several loops across the validators as in the spec.

This should collect all the info needed to implement:
- get_block_support_between_slots
- get_current_target_score
- get_adversarial_weight
- compute_empty_slot_support_discount

From the spec:
- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4747

In this PR, the goal is to capture everything related to the canonical
branch. get_current_target_score is out of scope for this PR as it also
needs data from non-canonical branches.

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Only update proposer boost if proposer is same as on canonical chain (#8104)
body:
From https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4807:

> There's a few changes. Firstly, there's a fix to the mechanism for
> setting the proposer boost root: we only update it if
> `block.proposer_index` matches the expected proposer of your current
> `head_state`. This way you can't nullify proposer boost by just
> creating forks with a divergent proposer sequence. Also small refactor
> with the updating logic moved to `update_proposer_boost_root`, and the
> block timeliness logic in `record_block_timeliness`. All of this is
> essentially unrelated to epbs.

Having to pull a fresh EpochRef is unfortunate, the existing one given
to `process_block` is not necessarily compatible with the canonical one.
Should be cached, though.

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Track inactive validators for fast confirmation rule (#8084)
body:
* Track inactive validators for fast confirmation rule

Validators that become inactive between the balance source snapshot
being taken and the current/prev/prev-prev epoch no longer have any
duties in some of these epochs. Rebase stored info to 1 instead of 0;
0 = inactive (default initialized), 1-32 = slot into epoch offset by 1.

Likewise for validators that become active _after_ the snapshot. For
these, we'll have to track the effective balances too, as EB is already
tracked while the validator is still inactive.

* Fix dst len < src len case

* Fix typos

subject: Match get_block_support_between_slots over-count from FCR spec (#8109)
body:
* Match get_block_support_between_slots over-count from FCR spec

In Fast Confirmation Rule specs, `get_block_support_between_slots`
ignores the slot at which a validator actually voted, and solely
looks at the committee assignment. It then over-counts support even
if the validator actually voted outside the requested range. This was
confirmed in the PR discussion to be intentional and safe. Update the
Nimbus implementation to match the counting behaviour of the spec.

- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4747

* Add tests for over-count situations

* Update test imports

author: Etan Kissling
subject: is_confirmed_chain_safe scaffolding for fast confirmation rule (#8121)
body:
Collect all the data needed for the various `is_one_confirmed` checks
needed during chain reconfirmation as part of `is_confirmed_chain_safe`:

- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4747

Compared to the specs, we do a simple pre-processing with a simplified
fork choice to collect just what's necessary (bounded) and then access
what's needed with O(1) accessors, rather than using nested loops.

`is_one_confirmed` is still a stub for now, but we now also reset the
confirmation rule if the `confirmed.root` is no longer a descendant of
`current_epoch_observed_justified.checkpoint`. Should not be reached in
a finalying scenario, and even if reached, the `fork_choice.nim` applies
the current mainnet rules (track greatest justified checkpoint) without
involving `is_confirmed_chain_safe` verdicts.

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Restart confirmation chain as needed by fast confirmation conditions (#8072)
body:
* Restart confirmation chain as needed by fast confirmation conditions

`get_latest_confirmed` defines a combination of conditions under which
the confirmation chain is restarted from the current epoch observed
justified checkpoint:

- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4747

Add the checks, both for when epoch advances (first check), and when
head changes. Should not trigger under finalizing (safe) conditions,
and if it does, gets overwritten by current mainnet logic of simply
tracking the justified checkpoint anyway.

* Also apply attestations before checking for FCR reset

* current_slot_head can only be updated before attestation deadline

* Re-run fork choice on epoch boundary before FCR reconfirmation

* Forward declaration

also allow displaying of safe block via `--status-bar-contents`.

Example config:

build/nimbus_beacon_node \
    '--status-bar-contents=peers: $connected_peers;finalized: $finalized_root:$finalized_epoch;safe: $safe_root:$safe_epoch:$safe_epoch_slot;head: $head_root:$head_epoch:$head_epoch_slot$next_consensus_fork;time: $epoch:$epoch_slot ($slot);sync: $sync_status|ETH: $attached_validators_balance'

* Fix type

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Remove weight of invalid blocks from ancestors (#8140)
body:
When a node is invalid, it gets filtered as unviable head when running
fork choice. But we still apply its weight to ancestors. To match the
optimistic vs lockstep behaviour, force weight of invalid blocks to 0,
regardless of proposer boosts or pre-existing votes, and remove the
weight from ancestors via the propagation mechanism.

author: Etan Kissling
subject: is_one_confirmed (#8130)
body:
Primary function of the Fast Confirmation Rule:

- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4747

Uses the various caches to efficiently determine `is_one_confirmed`
verdict, and call it from the reconfirmation path at epoch boundaries
to determine whether confirmation rule has to reset to finalized.
This function will eventually also be used to advance confirmation.

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Avoid SSZ codec depending on Altair (#8203)
body:
To use `get_generalized_index`, altair.nim needs to import SSZ, but SSZ
currently depends on the ParticipationFlags types of altair.nim.
Moving these types to base cleans up the dependencies.

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Limit state download size to 3 GB (#8206)
body:
* Limit state download size to 4 GB

SSZ is about 300 MB, JSON about 900 MB, 4 GB is plenty and gives us some
reasonable bound beyond the 6 minute timeout. This hardens the regular
--external-beacon-api-url further, where the idea is to only rely on the
server for data availability but not necessarily integrity.

* 3 GB instead of 4, for uint32

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Early reject data with incorrect fork digest (#8204)
body:
After reading response data, check that the given ForkDigest actually
matches the expected ConsensusFork, same as how these checks are already
done for light client data. For example, a Fulu block mislabeled as an
Electra block. Note: This still allows forkdigests from conflicting blob
schedules through, which is intentional, as a block can still be valid
according to our local forkdigest, we can just relabel it when others
request it from us.

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Cache participating balances from unrealized finality computation (#8216)
body:
* Cache participating balances from unrealized finality computation

When block is received, we have to run a partial epoch transition to
obtain unrealized finality checkpoints. As part of this, participating
balances info is computed. Later, when the epoch transition triggers,
we compute the participating balances a second time, on the same data.
Add a small cache for that to save ~10ms of epoch processing time.

* Add warning + metric to detect L2 cache incorrectness

* Add debugGloasComment to remember to remove the verification

* Additional helper to match put/find pattern

* Require exact slot match

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Add gindex constants for Gloas light client (#8327)
body:
Two changes:

(1) ePBS made the execution data in the BeaconBlock optimistic, it is
    not canonical until later in the slot when confirmed by the PTC.
    Sync committee signs earlier though, so light client data can no
    longer rely on BeaconBlock data for execution headers.

(2) Submarine where they replaced ExecutionPayload with just the block
    hash, meaning even for basics like block number or gas usage, one
    has to pay for another API call (either $ with provider, or latency
    with portal). Not a complicated change, but we have to re-root the
    Capella and Deneb execution proofs when migrating to Gloas.

Define the constants for now, this doesn't break anything and ensures
that we know when something becomes inconsistent in Heze etc.

subject: Revamp newPayload calls to enable light client based flow (#8329)
body:
* Revamp newPayload calls to enable light client based flow

Light client doesn't have access to the beacon block, so needs to use an
alternate flow to obtain the various components for engine_newPayload.
To support that, revamp the newPayload logic so that one can source the
components differently, while still reusing the same interaction logic.

Light client would then fill in:

- envelope and requests from envelope gossip
- versioned hashes from envelope.transactions (helpers_el.nim logic)
- parent hash either from envelope (if PR accepted), or deferred from
  light client headers, as we historically had in optimistic_processor.

* Cleanup v3/v4 (same args)

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Set --sync-light-client-finality=true by default in standalone LC (#8376)
body:
When using `nimbus_light_client`, we don't have a meaningful finalized
block hash to send to the EL. Because the light client 'finalized' has
lower security than the regular 'finalized' from a full node, so far we
opted to send `ZERO_HASH` on `engine_forkChoiceUpdated` in this mode,
with an opt-in flag to choose the finalized head from the LC data.

Change to opt-out, as sending an actual finalized head is very useful
for common EL sync scenarios. Users can pick the previous behaviour
by explicitly setting the flag to false.

author: Jacek Sieka
subject: avoid blocking main thread on reconstruction (#8346)
body:
* avoid blocking main thread on reconstruction

When running column reconstruction, the current approach blocks until
timeout or the reconstruction is finished, delaying other processing
that should be happening at the same time.

With a TSP, we can allow async processing to continue while the
reconstruction is done in the background also taking care to not stuff
the thread pool with tasks (since it's shared).

Further work is needed to enable reconstruction, in particular:
* Reconstruction should likely not run in onSlotEnd, ie it should
probably start somewhere close to the arrival of 50+% of the columns
* As reconstruction is running, we might receive columns from the
network - we should top up the known colums before creating new tasks so
as to avoid unnecessary recomputations
* We should be distributing the computed columns incrementally on the
network instead of just saving them to the DB - this of course relies on
computing them earlier - care must be taken to not start this process
"too" early, ie before a new head has been established by sufficient
attestations..

* oops

* lint

* better wait ordering

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Add config option for controlling LC data backfill (#8445)
body:
* Add config option for controlling LC data backfill

As a first step towards enabling peers to backfill historical LC data in
a trust-minimized way, add a debug flag that toggles activation, default
off for any user-facing instantiations, and default on for all tests.

The eventual protocol will involve these steps:

1. Sync a LightClientStore (either light client or full node)
2. When period P+1 finalizes, fetch LightClientPeriodData for P, with:
   - first_header: BeaconBlockHeader corresponding to block_roots[0]
   - finality_transition_pre: Last block with finalized cp pre P start,
     block_roots[8191] if did not finalize during P, default for genesis
     (header, finalized_checkpoint, finality_branch)
   - finality_transition_post: First block with finalized cp in P,
     has finality_transition_pre as parent (or 0 if genesis as parent),
     default if finality_transition_pre is block_roots[8191]
     (header, finalized_checkpoint, finality_branch)
   - block_roots: All block_roots of P
   - current_sync_committee: Sync committee for P (if post-altair)
   - current_sync_committee_branch: Proof relative to state_roots[8191]
   - latest_state_root: state_root after slot 8191 into P
   - latest_state_root_branch: Proof relative to htr(state_roots)
   - historical_summary_branch: HistoricalSummary can be recovered from
     block_roots + latest_state_root + latest_state_root_branch. This
     proofs htr(HistoricalSummary) relative to optimistic_update.header.
   - optimistic_update: Reduced version of best known LightClientUpdate
     for P+x with x >= 1 but as small as possible, makes it canonical
3. Assumption, client has full knowledge of periods > P from backfill
   or from local full node import. Verify optimistic_update is best, if
   P+1 is final, alternatively have to re-fetch later for canonical best
4. Fetch LightClientBlockData for post-altair epochs in P, with:
   - slot: Slot within P for this chunk, see block_roots[s % 8192]
   - sync_committee_bits: Part of the BeaconBlockBody
   - sync_committee_bits_branch: Proof relative to block_roots[s % 8192]
5. Verify answer is exhaustive (nothing withheld). For initial epoch,
   consult first_header from skeleton to see if it is in period < P and
   expected to be withheld when requesting P data
6. We can now run is_better_update from spec with LightClientBlockData
   and finality_transition_pre/post to identify canonical best update
7. Use light_client_updates_by_range/1 to obtain update for P,
   verify that it is canonical best. We can seal it, it cannot improve
8. Fetch LightClientBootstrapData for period P, response is list of:
   - header: LightClientHeader corresponding to block_roots[epoch_start]
     which may be in period < P, so cannot be bundled with the
     LightClientBlockData (only contains epochs in P, maybe newer fork)
   - current_sync_committee_branch: Proof of current_sync_committee in
     LightClientPeriodData relative to header.beacon.state_root
9. This reconstructs all LightClientBootstrap within period P, allowing
   peers to initiate sync from any historical checkpoint

Step 4-6 could be skipped by enshrining is_better_update into the STF,
would also reduce block_roots need to just the epoch transition blocks
with proofs relative to htr(block_roots). If proposed protocol becomes
too complex / too heavy, could try revive it, but not needed for now.

- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3614

* Default arg

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Remove EngineApiRole configuration (#8452)
body:
The EL roles feature from #4465 was never implemented or documented,
only the BN roles feature shipped. The three original EL roles were:

- DepositSyncing --> not relevant anymore since Electra
- BlockValidation --> normal operation
- BlockProduction --> kinda weird as a standalone, implies validation

Notably, this doesn't align with the way how external MEVboost works,
and also doesn't align with the ePBS work from Gloas where production
can be outsourced over the decentralized marketplace.

As EL roles never advanced past the config parsing stage, and this
feature wasn't documented or advertised, just drop it for now.
It wasn't used for >3 years.

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Avoid debug log defect when receiving block older than backfill (#8463)
body:
When a block's parent_root points to a pre-finalized slot during regular
forward sync, we mark it as unviable, as it does not descend finalized
history (#3478). For pre-backfilled slots, that would happen implicitly
via the `dag.getBlockRef(blck.parent_root)` logic -> MissingParent, and
then because it's pre-finalized would be marked unviable lateron.

In #5169, the checks for "trivial conditions" were moved earlier, not
sure if intentionally as it was possibly accidental re-indent noise.
That left a reference to `existing.get()` in the debug log, which is
also logged when `existing.isNone`, so triggers ResultDefect in debug.
Fix the log, and keep the UnviableFork treatment from #5169 in place.

subject: Revert "Apply KZG check to columns fetched via Req/Resp (#8458)" (#8464)
body:
This reverts commit 8b56bbcfbe9b05e5ab6d85f5c0dff7db5b5ace38.

In the original PR #8458 I overlooked the flow in block_processor that
already contains the KZG check (at a later stage). It's not perfect, as
it penalizes the incorrect peer (the one who sent the block, instead of
the one that sent us the bad column), and because it allows quarantine
pollution with bad data, but the check is indeed there! Double checking
just for minor benefits in peer score accounting is too expensive.
Should revisit later with a proper solution to avoid double-checking,
ideally with a type-system approach similar to blocks.

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Add `parent_block_root` to bid filtering key (#8510)
body:
The gossip rule was changed from:

> [IGNORE] This bid is the highest value bid seen for the corresponding
>          slot and the given parent block hash

to:

> [IGNORE] this bid is the highest value bid seen for the tuple
>          (bid.slot, bid.parent_block_hash, bid.parent_block_root)`.

- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5001

This way, someone can't just abuse a reorg to bid a large amount on a
non-canonical branch to purge the canonical bid. Catch up with spec.

Further, clean up the `parentExecHash != bid.parent_block_hash` check
which is not from spec and rejected bids building on the timeline where
the parent block's payload was withheld, by tracking the bids in the
pool separately based on timeline.

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Init AttPool EpochRef every 1024 slots instead of every 1024 blocks (#8578)
body:
As preparation for persisting all DAG heads in DB across restarts,
prepare the initialization of the AttestationPool by extracting the
per-head work into a helper. The performance optimization of #1910
in periods of long finality is slightly adjusted to ensure that calling
the helper on extra heads produces monotonically increasing checkpoints.

Old logic fetches accurate checkpoints for the latest 256 blocks
(from the head), and also every 1024 blocks (from the finalized).

New logic retains the former (eventually becomes union across all heads)
and changes the second condition to the first block in each 1024 slot
interval. This still skips most of the state replays but makes it so
that if additional heads are imported, checkpoints increase at the same
slot in each ancestry, i.e., on the first block introducing a new branch
and at the first block entering a new 1024 slot interval.

Note that in situations that have lots of empty slots, this reduces
startup performance compared to the old logic which only counted blocks,
if there is nonfinality > 1024 slots (32 epochs, ~3.4 hours Mainnet).

body:
The --debug-invalidate-block-root flag allows users to prevent import of
blocks that become asynchronously invalid via engine_forkchoiceUpdated.
While we honor the flag during gossip validation to prevent importing
blocks into fork choice optimistically (potentially getting stuck on an
invalid justification), we currently don't apply it on initialization.

when loading the non-finalized portion of the chain, we instead reset
the head to its parent block (latest valid head).

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Reject bids with invalid prev_randao during gossip validation (#8609)
body:
* Reject bids with invalid prev_randao during gossip validation

When someone sends us a bid with invalid prev_randao but high value,
it kicks out the legitimate bid. The invalid one is also non-punishable
as it fails subsequent state transition by peers.

Add an extra reject rule to filter out invalid prev_randao, there is
only a single valid value for each parent block root, and we have
efficient functionality in the blockchain_dag to obtain correct RANDAO
without expensive state replays.

Also proposed for spec inclusion, but we'll need the rule regardless:

- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5360

Have moved this check to the end, because if the correct value has not
yet been cached (i.e., no valid bid received), we may have to load the
block from disk (once).

* Apply suggestion from @tersec

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Ensure verification conditions for bid are satisfied as proposer (#8606)
body:
* Ensure verification conditions for bid are satisfied as proposer

Spec requires the proposer to ensure that the verification conditions
in `process_execution_payload_bid` are satisfied in order to construct
the `signed_execution_payload_bid` field in `BeaconBlockBody`:

https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-alpha.10/specs/gloas/validator.md#signed-execution-payload-bid

As gossip validation uses some arbitrary head state and also misses
certain checks compared to the full verification conditions, bids that
passed gossip validation may become invalid when re-verified with the
correct state.

Re-verify external bid validity on proposal, and if invalid, fall back
to local block building.

* Apply suggestion from @tersec

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Update fast_confirmation event to latest spec (#8661)
body:
* Update fast_confirmation event to latest spec

Specs added a `current_slot` marker to the `fast_confirmation` event:

> The node has executed the fast confirmation algorithm.
> This event should be emitted every time the algorithm is run,
> regardless of whether the most recent confirmed block has changed
> since the previous run. block is the root and slot is the slot of the
> most recent confirmed block, and current_slot is the wall-clock slot
> at which the algorithm was executed.

- https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Events/eventstream

Interpreting "every time the algorithm is run" as "whenever any of the
data changed" to avoid redundant spam, and "wall-clock slot" as the slot
to which fork choice was updated (may be slightly behind / ahead based
on gossip clock disparity and lag spikes).

* Fix

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Clarify gossip limits (#8738)
body:
In the spec, Req/Resp was changed a while ago to state that readers must
not read more than max_compressed_len(n) bytes when processing framed
snappy responses:

- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4045

The function for this limit is originally defined for non-framed snappy,
but it leaves enough room to also support sensibly framed snappy, i.e.,
it is always possible to encode the response in a way so that it fits.

Still, this limit enables filtering data that is encoded maliciously,
with lots of empty padding bytes, zero-length frames etc, while also not
being too strict in case someone wraps subchunks of the response in
separate snappy frames.

Note that there is also the 10 second response limit that applies to the
entire chunk, so without this, it's also not unbounded how much spam
can be sent.

author: Etan Kissling
subject: RPC chunks with stricter DOS limits where possible (#8744)
body:
Extra bytes beyond the `n` SSZ bytes in a Req/Resp request are required
to invalidate the prior request:

- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/1606

Should be fine on all of Mplex, Yamux and Quic, i.e., the protocol
requires the sender to explicitly half-close their end of the stream,
so we can always read the EOF explicitly on the reading end.

If there's a disconnect between the end of the request or the EOF,
the regular 10 second read timeout would eventually hit.

Impact is potentially a tiny higher latency before requests are answered
as we wait for 1 more signal that may or may not be combined with the
last request byte.

Closes #8435

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Avoid duplicate fcU sending (#8799)
body:
While light client is significantly ahead, its head overrides the head
from forward sync when interacting with the ELs. That forward sync still
triggers fcU periodically, though, which all get overridden with the
same head information, leading to exact duplicates being sent.

This is changed to only send one duplicate per slot (still needed as the
EL may be restarted or replaced in-between fcU calls). Also fix a race
when switching over from the LC head to the forward sync head, where two
fcU could be in flight simultaneously.

Closes #8041

> we lift only those locals that appear in more than one state

Therefore, the `let sigsets = batch[].multiSets.combineAll(verifier)`
variable is only present in the stack, as it is not used anymore after
the `await signal.wait()` further down.

To fix that, either we have to directly take an `addr` (or via template)
but because we only do `baseAddr sigsets` it doesn't extend lifetime
as that's just a regular `func` in stew.

Moving the section that converts the seq to unchecked array into the
task fixes this, as the `task` is still used after the `await`.

Impact here is that some batch verifies may end up reporting a wrong
result, and then fallback to the individual sig check. But we use refc
so it's not deterministically hit.

https://github.com/nim-lang/Nim/issues/26041

* Create the UncheckedArray on the main thread

* Just access sigsets to make the compiler think it's used across awaits

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Offload gossip KZG verifications to taskpool (#8810)
body:
While processing KZG isn't as heavy as BLS, the timing of KZG gossip
overlaps with attestation duties (Fulu) / payload attestations (Gloas).
As soon as we received enough columns, the head event is sent to the VC
but remaining data columns are still streaming in, potentially slowing
down the submission of attestations, e.g., this should help with #7981.

As we already have the infrastructure for offloading the cryptographic
verification work for other gossip topics, it's straightforward to just
reuse the same machinery for KZG proofs. It's a bit simpler than BLS as
we don't batch across columns, but follows the same flow.

and getBlockSlotId actually supports looking them up.

Allow querying by recent state roots (8192, based on head BeaconState)
and fix error code which should be 404 if not found instead of 500.
The functionality is available, just not exposed.

We still can't provide these APIs for historical states, but they are
available by slot. Further, only canonical states according to fork
choice are available by state_root.

Closes #7832

> Time series that are not present until something happens are difficult

first time where they are incremented.

author: Barnabas Busa
subject: Add version envelope to Gloas event stream events (#8816)
body:
The `execution_payload_bid`, `payload_attestation_message` and
`proposer_preferences` event stream topics are specified to wrap their
payload in a versioned envelope:

  data: {"version":"gloas","data":{...}}

but were emitted as the bare object instead. The generic `eventHandler`
calls `prepareJsonStringResponse`, whose only version-writing overload is
constrained to `SomeForkedLightClientObject`; every other queue falls
through to `RestJson.encode` and loses the envelope.

Wrap the three queues in `RestVersioned[T]` as the light client queues
already do, and add a matching `prepareJsonStringResponse` overload for
the Gloas event payloads. The fork is derived from the bid slot, the
payload attestation data slot and `proposal_slot` respectively rather
than hardcoded.

`EventProposerPreferencesObject` existed only to emit `{"data":...}` and
is superseded by `RestVersioned`.

Consumers relying on the envelope currently fail to decode these events;
Lighthouse, Teku and Grandine all emit the specified form.

Ref: https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/master/apis/eventstream/index.yaml

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Refresh VC duties when 'head' event reports new dependent roots (#8877)
body:
* Track latest attester / proposer dependent roots in VC

The VC now tracks which dependent root was used most recently for duties
updates, so that reorgs that solely drop duties without adding new ones
can also be logged, i.e., when a proposer duty is scheduled but later
dropped by a reorg, the reorg message now also shows up, whereas before
the log would only display when the duty gets _replaced_ by a new one.

The new fields also enable a future PR to react to new dependent roots
from the event stream, which since #8875 tracks the 'head' events that
contain dependent root information.

* Refresh VC duties when 'head' event reports new dependent roots

* Only invalidate if we have validators

* Also invalidate duties when validator indices update

* Also invalidate sync committee duties on validator index update

* Duty -> Duties terminology

* Also invalidate duties when re-connecting to event stream

* Also invalidate duties when there is an error requesting them

* In event mode, only poll duties once per epoch or when invalidated

* Move selection proofs loop out of attester / sync duty loops

* Trigger re-poll on subnet subscription failure

* Consistent ordering

* Avoid unnecessary future creation if event already set

* Cancel selection proofs task if it gets stuck longer than a slot

* Run attester / sync selection polling in parallel

* Fix edge case when attester duties modify during selections fill

* Fix edge case when polling runs across epoch boundary

* Fix cancellation

* Ensure slotSig / proof consistent, either write both or none

* Inline raceWithEvent helper

* Restore skipping of poll if work from earlier slot over-runs

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Define database API for LC data backfill (#9147)
body:
Add the database backend for the experimental LC data backfill protocol.
LightClientBackfillData is internal type to avoid having to update data
when transitioning into a new period (we don't know earlier which epoch
data has to include the sync committee).

New table only created with `--debug-light-client-data-import-backfill`.

- https://hackmd.io/@etan-status/decentralized-cl-sync

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Store full finalized_checkpoint in CachedLightClientData (#9161)
body:
For the experimental LC data backfill protocol, we'll need to collect
the `finalized_checkpoint.root`. Cache the full `Checkpoint` so that
we have that information available (reusing the `ref` approach that
we already use for the `current_period_best_update`, as checkpoints
don't change frequently).

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Fix LC logic when ALTAIR_FORK_EPOCH = 0 and initial epochs all empty (#9168)
body:
When initial epochs are completely missed, finalized_checkpoint can
update to the genesis block advanced to a later epoch, i.e., the
finalized_checkpoint.root changes from ZERO_HASH to genesis block hash.

Fix corresponding light client logic to support this situation.
Doesn't affect Mainnet, as Altair was not scheduled at genesis.

- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5707

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Handle restart when first slot of finalized epoch was missed (#9276)
body:
When first slot of finalized epoch is missed, the finalized checkpoint
block is from a prior epoch. When node is restarted, we initialize the
finalizedEpoch from the finalized checkpoint block's slot's epoch, which
is incorrect. When we then advertise this as a STATUS message, other
peers verify whether our finalized_root is the last block at or before
our advertised finalized_epoch.start_slot. As finalized_block.slot is
after that, we get disconnected by other peers who see that STATUS.

Change init logic to initialize finalized_epoch based on finalized_block
advanced to the next epoch boundary. Also fix AttestationPool init to
a proper value as fast confirmation rule logic expects that, and clean
up fork choice init logs the print the proper fork choice checkpoints.

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Implement gossip rule to ignore multiple blocks from same proposer@slot (#9280)
body:
We were missing implementation for this beacon block gossip rule,
slowing down recovery from certain non-finality scenarios:

> [IGNORE] The block is the first block with valid signature
>          received for the slot and proposer

- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-beta.4/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#beacon_block

Thanks to @Giulio2002 for the report.

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Avoid ignoring bids for second Gloas payload building on Fulu (#9263)
body:
When the second Gloas payload builds on top of the last Fulu payload
(e.g., the first Gloas payload was unavailable), we can't reliably get
parent gas limit as that's in Fulu, unless we load the full block (DB).

The forkyState.data.latest_execution_payload_bid.gas_limit value is
wrong in that situation, so we'd ignore correct bids. And when Gloas
finalizes, the value isn't used anymore because we then have the info.
Drop the check to avoid risk around the fork transition. If we forward
erroneously, it might lead to others ignoring it, but not rejecting.

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Handle STATUS message with finalized_epoch > head_slot.epoch (#9277)
body:
* Handle STATUS message with finalized_epoch > head_slot.epoch

If the first slot of epoch was missed, the `Checkpoint` for that epoch
contains a block root from an earlier epoch. When someone initializes
with checkpoint sync from that Checkpoint, their STATUS message is:

- finalized_root: Checkpoint.root
- finalized_epoch: Checkpoint.epoch
- head_root: Checkpoint.root
- head_slot: Checkpoint.root's corresponding block slot

Because Checkpoint.root is from an earlier epoch (as Checkpoint.epoch's
initial slot was missed), this means head_slot.epoch < finalized_epoch.
Handle that case and don't reject fresh checkpoint synced peers.

* Implement check for finalized epoch against wall clock

Add error handling for finalized epoch exceeding wall clock

Co-authored-by: Copilot Autofix powered by AI <175728472+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Use correct fork for sending ProposerPreferences at transition (#9289)
body:
For validators running inside the beacon node, when transitioning from
a fork to the next, ProposerPreferences are sent an epoch early, e.g.,
the HEZE_FORK_EPOCH ones are sent during the last Gloas epoch.

These were signed with the current epoch's fork. Correct this to sign
them with the correct proposal epoch instead. Also start sending in the
last Fulu epoch, as the validator client does.

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Cache PTC in EpochRef (#9341)
body:
Payload attestation messages need to look up the PTC depending on the
branch that they arrive on, which may have different PTC shufflings,

simply returns none.

author: 唐鳳
subject: fix: preserve execution budget for early Fulu blocks (#9329)
body:
## Problem

An admissible Fulu block can arrive shortly before its slot starts.
During the
preceding slot's last second, `nextSlotDeadline` derives a cutoff that
has
already elapsed and returns zero. The Engine API request can then be
cancelled
before a response is available. The cached absent result is subsequently
consumed as not validated.

For example, a block arriving 400 ms before slot S currently gets a
cutoff
1 second before S, rather than a usable execution budget for S.

## Change

Use the block slot for Fulu's early execution check and direct-storage
path.
Clamp the deadline slot to `[wallSlot, wallSlot + 1]` before converting
it to
time. This keeps old/current-block behavior, prevents an arbitrary
future slot
from creating an unbounded wait, and leaves other fork paths unchanged.

This does not change validity decisions, admission checks, cancellation,
retry,
or cache policy.

## Verification

- The new early-slot regression fails against the original arithmetic
and
  passes with this change.
- Deterministic tests cover early arrival, exact slot start, current and
late
  blocks, the cutoff and its immediate neighbors, and `FAR_FUTURE_SLOT`.
- All three deadline tests pass on both minimal and mainnet presets.
- The full mainnet `test_block_processor` suite passes: 15/15.
- The minimal suite is 11/15. Four unchanged tests fail with the same
Bellatrix/Capella `FieldDefect` before and after this change: Reverse
order
block add & get, Multiple heads, Invalidate block root, and Invalidate
existing
  block root. None was edited, skipped, or disabled.
- `make -j4 nimbus_beacon_node` succeeds.

Test compilation used `./env.sh nim c -d:release -d:disableLTO
-d:const_preset=<preset> --out:<binary> tests/test_block_processor.nim`.
The full mainnet binary was run without a filter. Individual regressions
were
also run using the runner's exact `suite::test` names.

On the same mainnet node, without changing the execution client or
resource
limits, a before/after observation showed:

| Observation | Before | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Optimistic REST samples | 26/180 | 0/768 |
| Longest observed optimistic run | 22 seconds | 0 seconds |
| Early blocks examined | 24, all NOT_VALIDATED | 7 resolved before slot
start, all VALID |

The patched observation collected 768 samples at a one-second cadence
(768 seconds on the process monotonic clock). All 59
resolved blocks were VALID, finalized epoch advanced by two, and there
were no
API errors, EL-offline samples, logged errors, or process restarts.
There were
15 brief syncing samples with maximum sync distance one slot. These are
observations from one node, not a general performance guarantee.

Checked `stable`, `testing`, and `unstable` before submission: each
still uses
the wall-slot-only helper.

---------

Co-authored-by: Etan Kissling <etan@nimbus.team>

author: Etan Kissling
subject: Switch CI to nimbus-common-workflow (#9388)
body:
Replace the custom build jobs in ci.yml with nimbus-common-workflow,
reducing duplication. Jobs and settings stay the same as before, except
that Windows now builds with LLVM 20 instead of 17.

- UBSan (for hashes starting with 7) runs as its own job in parallel
- Compiler command lines are hidden from the build output (Nim hints,
warnings and errors still show)
- Each job is a single step with its phases as log groups: different UI
